clue.text: Material taken by Technical College as gossip

parts.note: tabby is a watered silk fabric
CAT is short for College of Advanced Technology

explanation.surface: Someone takes fabric to a college and it becomes the talk of the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' just sets the material in front of the college. In old slang a tabby, or tabby-cat, was a spiteful gossiping woman, usually an old maid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabby-cat was an old name for a tattling, spiteful old woman, so it means a scandalmonger.

clue.text: Assign a late pass to return inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the letters of the other

parts.note: A plus late, taken as written

indicators.note: to return means the word for pass is read backwards

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone hands out a late pass so a straggler can get back indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses the pass, and 'inside' puts it within A LATE, giving A L-LOC-ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot or apportion something is to hand it out as a share.

clue.text: Abused defensive chess-player

parts.note: one side in chess is Black
guarded means wary and defensive

explanation.surface: A chess-player, put on the back foot, is treated badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order, chess-player first. To blackguard someone is to revile them in abusive language.
explanation.definitionFit: To blackguard is to revile in scurrilous language, so blackguarded means reviled or insulted.

clue.text: Hermetic (?) sign used by French noble in strange cause

indicators.note: in places the noble inside the jumbled letters
strange signals the word cause is jumbled into an odd new order

parts.note: a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat uses a mysterious symbol for an odd purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges CAUSE to CA...EUS, and 'in' puts DUC between. The caduceus is the winged staff of Hermes, hence 'Hermetic', with the (?) owning up to the pun on sealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent-twined winged staff carried by the god Hermes is his emblem.

clue.text: He takes lessons from the race-riot

indicators.note: riot suggests letters thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man learns something from a race riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race-riot' reads as one word, but 'riot' is the anagram signal for THE RACE. 'Takes lessons' means conducts them, not attends them.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster takes a class, meaning leads it, so he takes lessons in the sense of giving them.

clue.text: Implement with which to. apply butter?

definitions.text: Implement with which to. apply butter?

parts.words: Implement with which to. apply butter?
parts.note: butter here is flattery, and the idiom says flattery is laid on thickly with a bricklayer's tool

explanation.definitionFit: A bricklayer's flat-bladed tool is used to spread mortar, and flattery is said to be laid on with one.

clue.text: Boss uses telephone system to trap upstart

indicators.note: to trap means the letters for the telephone system enclose the other piece

parts.note: STD, subscriber trunk dialling, was the British direct-dial phone system
the start of up is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boss uses the phones to catch an upstart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstart' is read as 'up' start, giving U. STD was the old British trunk-dialling system.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a raised ornamental knob, which is one sense of a boss.

clue.text: Nancy, made topless, is so embarrassed — going blue in the face

indicators.note: embarrassed suggests letters thrown into confusion
made topless says the word Nancy loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nancy, caught without her top, is so mortified she changes colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made topless' takes the first letter off NANCY to leave ANCY; 'embarrassed' then rearranges ANCY with IS SO. The surface wants a blush, but the colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanosis is a bluish discoloration of the skin caused by lack of oxygen.

clue.text: Quixotic conduct

parts.note: Don Quixote set out as a wandering knight seeking adventures

explanation.definitionFit: Knight-errantry is the roving adventure-seeking of a knight, as Don Quixote practised it.

clue.text: Whence exile was able to make a come-back

indicators.note: to make a come-back means the word able is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exiled leader was capable of returning from his island.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was exiled to Elba in 1814 and escaped to make his famous return, so the surface itself is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island was the place Napoleon was banished to in 1814.

clue.text: Lay official pipe

explanation.definitionFit: A parish officer chosen from the laity, and also a long-stemmed clay tobacco pipe.

clue.text: His dexterity a mainstay?

parts.note: dexterity is read literally as right-handedness, and a mainstay is an indispensable helper

explanation.definitionFit: A chief assistant is relied on like the dexterous hand.

clue.text: Boatman may object to a horse

parts.note: to bar is to forbid or object to
gee, or gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: A boatman might refuse a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: A bargee works a barge on the canals, which were once horse-drawn, so the horse belongs in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargee is someone who crews a canal barge.

clue.text: They are versed in processing the last of the glucose

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word the
processing suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something is well-informed about how the end of the glucose is processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of the' gives E, and 'processing' rearranges E with GLUCOSE. 'Versed' means written in verse, not knowledgeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclogues are short pastoral poems, so they are set in verse.

clue.text: Fall back on engineer apprentice before recess

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate
an apse is a vaulted recess in a church

explanation.surface: A trainee engineer slips back before taking a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into a former state.

clue.text: Apostate Frenchman horribly aged

parts.note: René is a French man's name

indicators.note: horribly signals the letters of aged are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who has aged badly has turned his back on his faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges AGED to finish the word; the surface's elderly Frenchman is really just a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a faith or cause, just as an apostate does.

clue.text: Sour one, in our view

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
to us means in our opinion

explanation.surface: Somebody is judged a sourpuss in our opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetous means vinegary, like acetic acid, so sour.

clue.text: Bodies representing motor trials

parts.note: motor is a car
court cases are trials

explanation.surface: Bodies serve as evidence in motoring prosecutions.
explanation.definitionFit: Carcases are dead bodies, especially of animals.

clue.text: Last month one new team arrives at final

parts.note: ult., ultimo, means last month in old business letters
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: new signals the letters of team are made over

explanation.surface: Last month a newly formed side reached the final.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimate means last or final in a series.

clue.text: When I lead, the Muses follow? That's stupid!

parts.note: as means when
there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A speaker claims to lead the Muses, and someone calls the idea foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' and 'follow' only set the order. The Muses of Greek myth numbered nine, a fact the clue relies on.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means as foolish as an ass.

clue.text: Unnecessary poverty associated with the French quarter

parts.note: need means want or poverty
les is the French plural for the
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Poverty in the French district need not exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not required.

clue.text: Heartless new pattern of snare

indicators.note: new indicates the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement
heartless says the middle letter of the word pattern is removed

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted new design for a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the central T of PATTERN to leave PATERN, which 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch in a snare.

clue.text: Shylock asked for news on it

definitions.text: Shylock asked for news on it

parts.words: Shylock asked for news on it
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice Shylock asks what news there is on a Venetian bridge and exchange

explanation.definitionFit: The bridge and business district of Venice is where Shylock asks 'What news on the' place.

clue.text: Yellow flag once recognized by most countries

parts.note: gold is a yellow colour
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A yellow flag was once widely recognized internationally.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary system backing currency with bullion was once accepted by most nations.

clue.text: What's on offer is less than this price

definitions.text: What's on offer is less than this price

parts.words: What's on offer is less than this price
parts.note: a special offer is a reduction on the shop's catalogue figure

explanation.definitionFit: The manufacturer's recommended selling figure is what discounts are measured against.

clue.text: Naomi is back without a single complaint

indicators.note: without signals one letter is taken away
is back means the name Naomi is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Naomi has returned without a single grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' turns NAOMI into IMOAN, and 'without' takes away I.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Seize goods or transport, following underworld lead

indicators.note: following says the transport comes after the word for the underworld, which leads

parts.note: Dis is the Roman underworld, or its god
a train is transport

explanation.surface: Someone seizes goods or transport after a lead from the criminal underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following underworld lead' puts DIS first. To distrain is a legal term for seizing goods for debt.
explanation.definitionFit: To distrain is to confiscate property in settlement of a debt.

clue.text: Extracts leader of captives held by old Jewish sect

indicators.note: held by means the sect's name encloses the first piece

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of ancient times

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of captives

explanation.surface: An extract tells how a leader of captives was held by an old Jewish sect.
explanation.walkthrough: The Essenes were the ascetic Jewish community linked to the Dead Sea Scrolls; 'held by' puts the captives' leader within their name.
explanation.definitionFit: Essences are concentrated extracts of a substance.
